skill_traces.query:
Andrew: Hey Audrey, hope you're doing good! So I've decided to take a break from work yesterday and check out a new cafe. It was a nice change and reminded me of how the great outdoors is always there to offer you peace. Here's a photo from my last hike - so serene! How's your month been so far?
Audrey: Hi Andrew! The cafe sounds great, and the hike pic's great! August's been eventful - I learned a new skill! It was really awesome, making sure they were pampered and happy. I've always loved caring for my pups, and now taking care of their grooming myself makes me closer to them. They look so cute post-grooming!
Andrew: Wow that's awesome! You're doing an amazing job taking care of your pups. Can you show me a pic of them after the grooming? I bet they look adorable!
Audrey: Here's a photo of them after their grooming - look how soft and fluffy they are!
Andrew: Wow, they look so cute and fluffy! You did such a great job. How did you do it so well? I've always wanted to learn dog grooming but never got the time.
Audrey: I took a dog grooming course and learned lots of techniques. Would you like to hear some tips?
Andrew: Of course! I'd love to hear some tips. It's something I've always been interested in.
Audrey: Grooming slowly and gently, paying attention to sensitive areas like ears and paws. And remember to stay patient and positive throughout the grooming process.
Andrew: Cool tips! I'll remember them if I ever get to groom Toby. Thanks!
Audrey: No problem, glad the tips helped. If you ever give it a shot, let me know and I can provide more advice.
Andrew: Thanks! I'll let you know if I decide to give it a try. Appreciate your help. What are your plans for the weekend?
Audrey: I'm taking them out for a stroll in the park - they love it and it's a good workout for us. Any weekend plans for you?
Andrew: This weekend I'm heading to a nature reserve to reconnect with the outdoors - excited!
Audrey: Cool! Have a great time reconnecting with nature. Don't forget to take some nice pictures!
Andrew: Sure thing, I'll get some awesome pics to show you when I return. 
Audrey: Haha thanks! Your pics of hikes are always nice.
Andrew: Yeah! I really wanted to save the moment ya know?
Audrey: No wonder. Now I can't wait for the pics. Take care and have fun! My dogs will be waiting too!
Andrew: Thanks! Can't wait to show you them when I'm back. See ya!

selected.name: Extract Photo-Sharing Events
selected.description: When a message presents an object or result with visual language like 'Here are...' or explicitly mentions sharing a photo, during extraction.
content: When a message uses presentation phrasing such as 'Here are...', 'Check out...', 'This is a photo of...', or 'Attached is...' to introduce something, record that the speaker shared a photo of that item, even if the word 'photo' does not appear.

If the speaker explicitly mentions sharing, sending, or showing a picture/photo/image, create an event memory that records the sharing action and the described content (e.g., subject or creator of the picture).
Preserve the literal object named in the message (e.g., picture) — do not replace it with an inferred object such as a bookshelf, item, or possession.
Keep the sharing act within the same event memory as the other facts from that message; do not summarize away the visual sharing.
Only include facts explicitly stated; do not convert a shared picture into an ownership claim unless ownership is directly stated.
selected.rerank_reason: The session contains explicit mentions of sharing photos, such as 'Here's a photo of them after their grooming' and 'I'll get some awesome pics to show you when I return,' which directly trigger the photo-sharing extraction procedure.

Preserve all distinct pieces of advice and their qualifiers; do not collapse or omit details. Tentative phrasing still counts.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Family Pet Ownership
nearby_not_selected.description: When a speaker references a pet as belonging to their family or household (including via a photo), during extraction.
content: During extraction, if a message links a pet to the speaker's own family or household (e.g., 'my family's dog', 'our dog', a photo described as my family's pet), create a memory that the speaker had that pet.
Do not require an explicit statement like 'I grew up with a dog'; owning a family pet in the past implies it was part of the speaker's upbringing.
Skip pet mentions that clearly belong to someone else (e.g., a friend's dog) or that are generic with no owner.
Record the speaker as subject and use event or relationship memory kinds as appropriate; stop after extracting the ownership fact—do not expand into extra searches or unrelated pet details.
